symptoms: Global route GRC overflow exceeding 5% localized entirely within narrow inter-macro channels, while surrounding core utilization is under 70%.
Detailed route DRC count exploding (>10,000 shorts and spacing errors) on lower metal layers (M1–M3) within high-density standard cell regions.
Pin access congestion report showing >1.5 unreachable pin access points per cell in dense 7nm FinFET standard cell clusters.

candidate_causes.cause: Over-dense standard cell placement around macro boundaries.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Query local placement density in a 10x10 GRC window; check if local utilization exceeds 85% near macro corners.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Apply partial placement blockages (50–60% max density limit) in inter-macro channels.

candidate_causes.cause: CTS buffer insertion inflating local cell density in narrow routing channels.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Filter instance list in congested GRCs by cell type; check if clock buffers/inverters constitute >30% of local cell area.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Define CTS buffer exclusion zones inside narrow channels and incremental-route clock nets.

candidate_causes.cause: High-fanout or bus routing traversing low-layer metal tracks across a narrow bottleneck.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Generate net flightline density report crossing the congested GRC boundary sorted by assigned metal layer.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Assign layer path constraints (e.g., target M5–M7) for long high-fanout bus nets.

candidate_causes.cause: Sub-optimal macro floorplanning creating narrow channels and convergent signal paths.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Examine macro pin orientations relative to opposite core logic; verify available track count vs required cross-channel net count.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Shift macro positions to widen channels by 15–30um or rotate macros to face pins toward open core.

ordering_rationale: Triage proceeds from fast static density queries to full net track analysis, prioritizing low-cost non-disruptive placement keepouts over expensive floorplan re-spins.
classic_trap: Treating macro channel routing track exhaustion as a global placement problem and lowering overall block utilization, which degrades timing across the entire block without solving the localized channel bottleneck.

symptoms: Massive uniform timing failures (hundreds to thousands of paths failing by near-identical magnitude matching half or full clock period).
Single-path topological failure where WNS is dominated by combinational logic depth (>25–30 logic levels).
Physical path detour failure where net delay accounts for >70% of total path delay across wide floorplan spans.

candidate_causes.cause: Missing or incorrect SDC constraint (e.g., missing clock groups or false path).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Inspect failure report profile: if thousands of failing paths originate across un-grouped clock domains and fail by near-identical large magnitudes, check SDC.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Correct SDC (add set_clock_groups -asynchronous or adjust multicycle path settings).

candidate_causes.cause: Excessive combinational logic depth in synthesized gate netlist.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Sort timing report by logic depth; cell delay dominates path delay (>60%) with >20 stages.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert pipeline stages in RTL or re-synthesize with tighter timing constraints.

candidate_causes.cause: Physical floorplan detachment (long wire placement detours between driver and load).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report physical net length and pin placement coordinates; net delay exceeds 60% of total delay due to placement split across die.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Apply regional placement bounds, group constraints, or align partition boundary port locations.

candidate_causes.cause: High clock skew or late capture clock arrival caused by CTS imbalance.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Inspect launch vs capture clock tree latency in path timing report; capture clock latency significantly lags launch clock.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-balance clock tree branches, adjust clock target latency, or apply useful skew.

ordering_rationale: Triage starts with diagnostic report inspection to immediately separate simple SDC errors from real physical or RTL logic bottlenecks before running physical optimization loops.
classic_trap: Assuming a massive block-wide setup WNS failure requires heavy physical re-optimization or buffer sizing when it is actually caused by a single unconstrained asynchronous clock domain crossing.

symptoms: Hold violations widespread across thousands of short paths (0–1 logic levels) with minimal launch clock delay.
Hold failures concentrated exclusively at cross-clock domain or cross-corner signoff interfaces.
Severe hold violations post-CTS caused by large negative clock skew between adjacent registers.

candidate_causes.cause: Extreme clock skew between launch and capture registers within the same clock branch.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Inspect timing report clock paths: launch clock latency is significantly shorter than capture clock latency (skew exceeds path data delay).
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-buffer clock tree branches or adjust CTS skew targets.

candidate_causes.cause: Fast-path zero-logic connections between registers placed in close physical proximity.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check timing report for zero combinational gates and driver Q to load D physical distance under 5um.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Allow P&R tool to auto-insert delay buffers during post-CTS/route hold fixing.

candidate_causes.cause: Mismatched PVT operating conditions across multi-corner signoff (e.g., fast-corner hold vs slow-corner setup).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare timing reports across signoff corners; hold violations exist strictly in fast/min-voltage corner.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Optimize hold fixing explicitly in the fast corner while monitoring slow corner setup slack.

candidate_causes.cause: Unconstrained or improperly budgeted cross-clock domain interface paths.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check launch/capture clock domain names in hold report; verify if false_path or min_delay constraints are applied.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add explicit set_false_path or set_min_delay constraints for asynchronous crossings.

ordering_rationale: Checks prioritize rapid inspection of path topology and clock skew in timing reports to distinguish benign fast paths (fixed automatically) from structural CTS skew or SDC errors.
classic_trap: Manually inserting hold delay buffers on short data paths before verifying CTS clock skew, which leads to area bloat and setup timing degradation if the clock tree is later re-balanced.

symptoms: Static voltage drop exceeding signoff threshold (>3–5% VDD) concentrated in central floorplan regions distant from power pads.
Dynamic IR drop spikes (>10–15% VDD) temporally aligned with simultaneous clock edge switching events.
Setup timing degradation or intermittent functional errors localized to high-density logic clusters during dynamic simulation.

candidate_causes.cause: Insufficient static power grid mesh density or missing top-layer power straps.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Run static IR drop analysis; voltage drop contour forms a smooth spatial gradient peaking in the die center away from PG pads.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add top-layer (M7/M8/RDL) power/ground straps and increase PG VIA density.

candidate_causes.cause: Localized dynamic switching current surge (high local dynamic power density).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Run dynamic vector-based IR analysis; drop correlates strictly with simultaneous clock edge switching of dense register banks.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: De-cluster register placement, stagger clock tree arrival times (clock skewing), or add decap cells.

candidate_causes.cause: Inadequate Decoupling Capacitor (Decap) cell allocation around high-toggle logic.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Map decap cell density against dynamic IR peak locations; confirm decap coverage is under 5% in high-drop regions.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Insert physical decap cells in available filler spaces around high-toggle cells and macro boundaries.

candidate_causes.cause: Macro power pin starvation (insufficient PG pin VIAs to power grid).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Perform PG resistance extraction on macro pins; check for high-resistance path from grid to macro VDD/VSS pins.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Add dedicated power rings or increase PG pin drop VIA density directly onto macro power tracks.

ordering_rationale: Triage begins with quick static grid resistance and decap density checks before investing in computationally heavy dynamic vector-based IR simulations.
classic_trap: Attempting to solve high dynamic IR drop by simply adding more static power straps, ignoring local simultaneous switching current surges that require decap allocation or clock edge staggering.

symptoms: Excessive clock skew (>200–500ps on a sub-nanosecond period) across sinks within the same clock domain.
Unusually high clock insertion delay (latency) accompanied by deep clock buffer trees (>15–20 buffer levels).
Severe clock power bloat where clock tree buffers consume >30–40% of total block dynamic power.

candidate_causes.cause: Unconstrained clock sinks or missing clock definition (non-register pins included in CTS).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report CTS sink list; check if non-register pins, memory control inputs, or combinational logic pins are listed as sinks.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Update CTS specification to mark non-clock pins as stop pins or ignore pins.

candidate_causes.cause: Placement blockages or macro obstacles blocking CTS trunk routing corridors.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Overlay clock buffer placement and routing against macro floorplan; observe long buffer detours around hard blockages.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Adjust placement blockages, create dedicated clock routing corridors, or relocate clock root pins.

candidate_causes.cause: Over-constrained CTS targets (unrealistically tight target skew forcing tool over-buffering).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Review CTS constraint file; check if target skew is set extremely tight (e.g., <10ps on a large FinFET block).
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Relax target skew to realistic signoff limits (e.g., 50–80ps) and enable useful skew.

candidate_causes.cause: High clock pin density or severe localized load imbalance.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Examine fanout and sink capacitance distribution per clock branch in CTS report; locate branches with >5x load disparity.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Clone clock buffers, restructure clock tree topology using H-Tree or mesh structures.

ordering_rationale: Triage checks CTS spec and constraint definitions first (which take minutes to inspect and fix) before re-synthesizing clock topologies or modifying physical corridors.
classic_trap: Trying to force tight clock skew by letting the CTS engine insert endless buffer stages, which dramatically increases clock latency, power, and dynamic IR drop.

symptoms: High-density DRC clusters (hundreds of short/spacing errors) confined within localized standard cell regions.
Off-grid pin access DRCs (pin connection unreachable without violating minimum line-end/spacing rules in 7nm/5nm FinFET).
Metal width, enclosure, or antenna DRC violations occurring systematically along long top-layer routing nets.

candidate_causes.cause: Cell pin access blockage in high-density FinFET nodes (insufficient hit points for M1/M2 routing).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Filter DRC report by violation type (Pin Access / Line-End Spacing); check if >80% occur on M1/M2 at standard cell boundaries.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Apply cell pin keepouts, use track-aligned cell placement, or reduce localized standard cell utilization.

candidate_causes.cause: Post-route manual ECO or uncoordinated net modification creating net overlaps.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Check DRC error log timestamps and net names against recent ECO netlists or manual wire edits.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Re-run incremental detailed route on modified nets with DRC-guided ECO router.

candidate_causes.cause: Inconsistent LEF/TECH LEF rule files between P&R tool and signoff DRC engine (e.g., Calibre vs P&R).
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Compare signoff DRC rule deck version against P&R tech file; run a 1-net test route to verify if P&R router considers geometry legal.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Update P&R technology files and LEF definitions to match signoff DRC deck.

candidate_causes.cause: Antenna rule violations on long nets traversing metal layers without diode protection.
candidate_causes.distinguishing_check: Report antenna ratio violations from signoff report; identify nets with high metal area-to-gate area ratio lacking antenna diodes.
candidate_causes.typical_fix: Auto-insert antenna diodes near load pins or force layer hopping to top metal layers.

ordering_rationale: Triage identifies whether DRCs are systematic rule/setup mismatches or localized physical pin-access issues before initiating full detailed route passes.
classic_trap: Repeatedly running detailed routing iterations expecting the P&R engine to resolve pin access DRCs in a 95% dense FinFET block, when the fundamental cause is pin grid misalignment requiring cell density reduction.
